meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What else do you have?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend, and kids paste from another file all the time. That shows where it was typed, not who wrote it.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever happens from here, nothing goes on his record and nothing happens in front of his class. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Editions differ, and a seventeen-year-old misremembering a line isn't fraud.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Then what exactly are you proposing, Hale?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their minds in two weeks; that's called learning. I asked what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, so I'll take it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. The rewrite before December 1, the zero gone from the gradebook, and nothing on his record. In writing tonight, Hale.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. I'll confirm with him tonight and answer your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of his class and before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that confirmed in writing, with the zero removed from the gradebook. I expect that confirmation in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Her last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants those terms confirmed in writing tonight and Owen's agreement to the date. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it well before her time ran out.
What moved her: When she said he could have pasted it from another file, you asked for a dated draft. That made the version history with its times stand as evidence she could check.
What cost ground: When she asked what you were proposing, you showed another document first. She had to repeat her demand, and she got sharper.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop. Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history, with all the writing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, landed right on that kind of night, and that is why she rushed to write the times down and argued about pasting. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what you were proposing after the quotation that wasn't in the play, put the 4.4 rewrite on the table right then instead of adding the outline.
